summary: Material changes since the prior snapshot: U.S. August CPI was released at +0.4% m/m and +3.4% y/y, with core CPI +0.3% m/m and +2.4% y/y; the core monthly reading was above Reuters-polled expectations of +0.2%. Official Treasury closing yields for September 11 rose to 4.63% at 2Y and 4.96% at 10Y. Middle East conflict transmission broadened through record VLCC freight from the Gulf of Oman to China near Worldscale 450, about US$11.50/bbl. Brent settled at US$104.61 and WTI at US$100.05. No new Taiwan official macro release was identified since the prior snapshot.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Higher U.S. real/nominal discount-rate risk and imported-energy/freight inflation remain headwinds for long-duration technology and energy-intensive sectors, while AI/HPC export demand remains a domestic growth offset.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Semantic interpretation is downstream research input only.

US_PCE_CORE_PCE.latest_official: July 2026: headline PCE +3.7% y/y; core PCE +3.3% y/y.

FED.market_context: Reuters reported roughly 85-87% pricing for a 25 bp rate increase after the CPI release, versus about 67-72% before it.

DXY.note: Reuters market observation; deterministic market-series ingestion remains authoritative.

USD_TWD.note: No September 11 close was inserted because a sufficiently authoritative same-day value was not verified in this run.

key_drivers.name: U.S. August CPI firms on energy and core services
key_drivers.observed: Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y. Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y; the core monthly reading exceeded the Reuters-polled 0.2% expectation. Gasoline rose 3.9% m/m and shelter 0.3%.
key_drivers.interpretation: The report strengthens the case for a near-term Fed hike and raises the discount-rate risk for high-duration Taiwan technology equities even though core year-on-year inflation eased slightly.

key_drivers.name: Official U.S. yield curve reprices higher
key_drivers.observed: Treasury's September 11 official par yields closed at 4.63% for 2Y and 4.96% for 10Y, a +33 bp 10Y-2Y slope.
key_drivers.interpretation: Both front-end policy expectations and long-duration discount rates are restrictive for Taiwan growth-equity valuation multiples.

key_drivers.name: Record Gulf-to-Asia tanker freight
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC freight near Worldscale 450, around US$11.50 per barrel, a record for the series introduced earlier in 2026.
key_drivers.interpretation: The Middle East shock is increasingly embedded in delivered-energy and logistics costs, not merely spot crude, raising imported inflation and margin risk for Taiwan manufacturers.

key_risks: A sustained U.S. 10Y yield near 5% can compress long-duration semiconductor and AI hardware valuation multiples.
Record tanker freight, war-risk premiums and constrained Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb flows can keep delivered energy costs elevated even if spot crude retreats.

Core PCE for August may be revised higher by CPI/PPI components; Reuters-cited economists expected about +0.3% m/m and 3.4% y/y, but this is an estimate and is not written into the official PCE series.
Taiwan's strong AI/HPC export cycle offsets but does not eliminate energy, FX and global-rate risks.
No new verified copper or September 11 USD/TWD close was inserted; those series remain stale in this semantic snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish risk increased after August CPI. No FOMC decision has occurred yet; the next meeting is September 15-16.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: No new decision. Imported-energy inflation, U.S. yields and FX pressures are more important ahead of the September 17 meeting, while exports remain strong.
policy_tone.global: Energy and freight shocks are keeping global monetary-policy risks hawkish while simultaneously increasing downside risk to real demand.

events.observed_evidence: Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC rates reached around Worldscale 450, roughly US$11.50/bbl, according to Reuters citing Baltic Exchange data.
events.semantic_interpretation: Physical shipping scarcity and war-risk pricing are broadening the inflation shock beyond crude oil itself.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters reported Houthi advances to Perim Island and Dhubab near Bab el-Mandeb and a temporary shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline after a drone attack.
events.semantic_interpretation: A second major shipping chokepoint is under greater threat while Hormuz flows remain constrained.
